chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me who said: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from Sulayman ibn Dawud who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Al-Zuhri who said: Ali ibn Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) said:

The most severe hours for the son of Adam are three: the hour in which he confronts the Angel of Death, the hour in which he rises from his grave, and the hour in which he stands before God, the Exalted, either to Paradise or to Hell,

then he said: If you are saved, O son of Adam, at the time of death, then you are saved, otherwise you are destroyed. If you are saved, O son of Adam, when you are placed in your grave, then you are saved, otherwise you are destroyed. If you are saved when people are carried over the Bridge, then you are saved, otherwise you are destroyed. If you are saved when people stand for the Lord of the Worlds, then you are saved, otherwise you are destroyed.
And before them is a barrier until the Day they are raised.
He said: It is the grave, and indeed for them therein is a hard livelihood. By God, the grave is indeed a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of Hell,

then he turned to a man from his companions and said to him: The Resident of the Heavens knows the Resident of Paradise from the Resident of Hell. Which of the two men are you, and which of the two abodes is your abode?

key_terms.حُفْرَةٌ مِنْ حُفَرِ النَّارِ: A pit from the pits of Hell
key_terms.رَوْضَةٌ مِنْ رِيَاضِ الْجَنَّةِ: A garden from the gardens of Paradise

ai.seo_question: What are the three most critical hours for a human being in the afterlife according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) identifies the moments of death, resurrection from the grave, and standing before God as the three most critical trials, emphasizing that survival in each stage determines one's ultimate fate. He links the grave to a state of hard livelihood and describes it as either a garden of Paradise or a pit of Hell, citing the concept of Barzakh. This narration highlights the continuity of the soul's journey and the significance of the intermediate realm in Shia eschatology.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-108 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Davood, on the authority of Abdul Raz’zaq, on the authority of Mu’amir, on the authority of Al-Zuhra that Ali ibn al-Hussein ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (Imam as-Sajjad (MGB)) said,

“The worst times for man are three: the time at which the angel of death comes to take his life; the time at which he is risen out of the grave; and the time at which he shall stand before the Honorable the Exalted God to see whether he shall go to Paradise or be taken into Hell.”

As-Sajjad (MGB) added, “O Children of Adam! If you are saved at the time of death, then you are saved. Else you shall be destroyed. If you are saved when you are being placed in the grave, then you are saved. Else you shall be destroyed. If you are saved when they are taking the people towards the Bridge , then you are saved. Else you shall be destroyed.”
Then As-Sajjad (MGB) recited the following verse of the Holy Quran: ‘…Before them is a Partition till the Day they are raised up.’
Then As-Sajjad (MGB) added, “This Partition refers to the grave in which life is hard. I swear by God that the grave can be one of the gardens of Paradise or one of the ditches of Hell!”

Then As-Sajjad (MGB) faced a man who was present there and said to him, “Indeed the Residents of the Heavens know the Residents of Paradise and the Residents of Hell! Which group do you belong to? With which of the two shall be your Final Abode?”
